title: Phone-controlled LED
intro: Make your own web page that turns an LED on and off from your phone.

wiring_steps.title: The LED
wiring_steps.text: Unplug the USB cable before you change any wires. Plug it back in when you're done. Start with the power rails: a black wire from GND on your board to the blue (−) rail at the bottom of the breadboard, and a red wire from {{VCC}} to the red (+) rail. Push the LED into holes H8 and H9, with the long leg (+) in H9. Put a 220Ω resistor from G8 across the gap to E8. Add a wire from {{pin:LED_PIN}} to J9, and a black wire from A8 to the blue (−) rail at the bottom.

steps.title: Make a hotspot
steps.text:
Your board can make its own WiFi network, just like a phone's hotspot. `WiFi.softAP(name, password)` starts it. The password needs at least 8 letters.

**Your task:** change the name to your own (like `ArduinoPath-Alex`), then Run or Upload. Look for it in your phone's WiFi list.
hints: Change `Sam` to your name, inside the quotes.
Keep the password 8 letters or longer, or the hotspot won't start.
The Serial Monitor shows the address to open: 192.168.4.1.

checks.label: I can see my hotspot on a phone

steps.success: Your board has its own WiFi network!

steps.title: Hello, web page
steps.text:
A **web server** answers when a browser asks for a page. `server.on("/", homePage)` says: when someone asks for the home page, run `homePage()`. It sends back **HTML**, the language of web pages.

Your board makes its **own WiFi network** (a hotspot). On your phone, open WiFi settings, join the network with your board's name, then open **192.168.4.1** in the browser. In the simulator, use the **phone panel**.

**Your task:** change the message on the page, then Run and open the page.
hints: `server.handleClient()` must run in `loop()`, or the page never loads.
On a phone, you must join the board's WiFi first.

checks.label: I saw my page on a phone (or the phone panel)

steps.success: You made a web page, served by your own board.

steps.title: ON and OFF buttons
steps.text:
Now the page has two buttons. Tapping **ON** asks for the page **/on**, which runs `turnOn()`.

**Your task:** fill in the blanks so the buttons work.
hints: Each page address needs a function to run.
`/on` runs `turnOn`. The other button's address is in the HTML.

checks.label: My phone turns the LED on and off

steps.success: You're controlling real hardware from your phone!

outro: Your board is a **web server**: your phone asks for a page, the board sends back **HTML**, and links like **/on** run your code. That's how smart lights and smart plugs work.
stretch: Add a Blink button that makes the LED flash 5 times.
Show whether the LED is on or off on the page.
Add a second LED with its own buttons.
